slides.title: Who does what?
slides.html:
Client–server

Who does what?

Client

The React app in the browser. Shows the UI and sends requests.

fetch("/api/jobs")

Server

Node + Express. Checks requests, runs logic, talks to the database.

app.get("/api/jobs")

Database

Stores data permanently. (MongoDB, next week.)

Job.find()

slides.title: Node.js and npm
slides.html:
Setup

Node.js and npm

  • Node runs JavaScript outside the browser
  • npm installs packages
  • package.json lists your project's packages
  • nodemon restarts the server when you save

Terminal

mkdir jobs-api && cd jobs-api
npm init -y
npm install express
npm install --save-dev nodemon
 
# package.json
"type": "module",
"scripts": {
  "dev": "nodemon server.js",
  "start": "node server.js"
}
 
npm run dev

slides.title: Your first Express server
slides.html:
Express

Your first Express server

  • app.get handles a GET request to a path
  • req: the request coming in
  • res: the response you send back
  • res.json sends JSON

server.js

import express from "express";
 
const app = express();
app.use(express.json());
 
app.get("/", (req, res) => {
  res.json({ message: "Jobs API is running 🚀" });
});
 
const PORT = process.env.PORT || 5000;
app.listen(PORT, () => {
  console.log(`Server on http://localhost:${PORT}`);
});

slides.title: REST API design
slides.html:
REST

REST API design

  • Resources are nouns: /api/jobs
  • The HTTP method is the verb
  • Return the right status code
  • Send JSON in and out

Jobs API

GET     /api/jobs        list all jobs        200
GET     /api/jobs/:id    get one job          200 / 404
POST    /api/jobs        create a job         201
PATCH   /api/jobs/:id    update a job         200
DELETE  /api/jobs/:id    delete a job         204
 
# not REST-y:
# GET /getAllJobs   POST /deleteJob?id=3

slides.title: Routes and controllers
slides.html:
Structure

Routes and controllers

routes/jobs.js

import { Router } from "express";
import * as jobs from "../controllers/jobs.js";
 
const router = Router();
 
router.get("/", jobs.list);
router.get("/:id", jobs.getOne);
router.post("/", jobs.create);
router.delete("/:id", jobs.remove);
 
export default router;

controllers/jobs.js

let jobs = [];
 
export const list = (req, res) => {
  res.json(jobs);
};
 
export const create = (req, res) => {
  const job = { id: Date.now(), ...req.body };
  jobs.push(job);
  res.status(201).json(job);
};

app.use("/api/jobs", jobsRouter)

slides.title: Middleware
slides.html:
Middleware

Middleware

  • Functions that run before your route
  • They can read, change or stop the request
  • Call next() to continue
  • Built-in, third-party (cors) or your own

server.js

import cors from "cors";
 
app.use(express.json());   // read JSON bodies
app.use(cors());           // allow your React app
 
// your own: log every request
app.use((req, res, next) => {
  console.log(req.method, req.url);
  next();
});

slides.title: Bodies, params and query strings
slides.html:
Requests

Bodies, params and query strings

  • req.body: data sent with POST/PATCH
  • req.params: parts of the path
  • req.query: after the ? in the URL

Reading the request

// POST /api/jobs { "title": "Dev" }
req.body.title           // "Dev"
 
// GET /api/jobs/42
req.params.id            // "42" (always a string)
 
// GET /api/jobs?location=Lagos&page=2
req.query.location       // "Lagos"
req.query.page           // "2"

slides.title: Error handling
slides.html:
Errors

Error handling

  • Validate input and return 400
  • Return 404 when something isn't found
  • One error middleware for everything else
  • Never crash the server or leak stack traces

server.js

export const getOne = (req, res) => {
  const job = jobs.find((j) => j.id === Number(req.params.id));
  if (!job) return res.status(404).json({ message: "Job not found" });
  res.json(job);
};
 
// last, after all routes
app.use((err, req, res, next) => {
  console.error(err);
  res.status(500).json({ message: "Something went wrong" });
});

slides.title: The update and delete controllers
slides.html:
Build

The update and delete controllers

  • Find the item by id
  • 404 if it isn't there
  • Return the right status

controllers/jobs.js

export const update = (req, res) => {
  const job = jobs.find((j) => j.id === Number(req.params.id));
  if (!job) return res.status(404).json({ message: "Job not found" });
  Object.assign(job, req.body);
  res.json(job);
};
 
export const remove = (req, res) => {
  const before = jobs.length;
  jobs = jobs.filter((j) => j.id !== Number(req.params.id));
  if (jobs.length === before)
    return res.status(404).json({ message: "Job not found" });
  res.status(204).end();
};
